correctness.rationale: Cheliotis--Papadatos give the exact quantile \(Q(u)=-\log(1-u)/u\). Substituting \(U=1-e^{-E}\) with \(E\sim\operatorname{Exp}(1)\) gives the representation exactly. Writing survival \(q\) gives \(x=-\log q/(1-q)\); differentiation yields the displayed hazard. Its sign derivative reduces to φ(L)=L-2+e^{-L}(L+2), whose derivative is \(1-e^{-L}(L+1)>0\) for \(L>0\). Thus the hazard is strictly decreasing on the whole support, with endpoint limits 2 and 1. The integer moments follow by the nonnegative expansion of \((1-e^{-t})^{-m}\), so monotone convergence justifies all termwise integrations. The packaged checker reproduces the formulas numerically but is not used as proof.

value.rationale: The source uses the maximal-average law for ruin probability and for alarm thresholds, so its hazard structure is directly meaningful rather than an arbitrary post-processing. Strict DFR gives a global qualitative classification of the entire law, showing that conditional exceedance intensity falls monotonically from 2 to the exponential-tail level 1. The complete integer-moment sequence supplies exact quantitative summaries, with the mean and variance collapsing to classical zeta constants. Together these form a natural structural characterization of the exact distribution, not a one-off numerical evaluation.
